nodes.label: D1 — Quantile-Winsorized Binning
nodes.rationale: Histogram over [Q(0.01), Q(0.99)] with out-of-range values clamped into edge bins, chosen because naive min-max collapses 99.735% under a single outlier vs 0.182% for winsorized (exp1). k-NN rejected as default despite passing the gate: differential entropy incompatible with [0,1] normalization, diverges to -inf on duplicates (ReLU zeros), O(N^2). Fixed range kept as explicit option. Documented costs: attainable max 99.92% of log B on continuous uniform-density data (asymmetric-quantile H* formula corrected after adversarial review, regressed in exp1); heavy-tailed (Cauchy) data 4-5x more seed-variable than fixed range — prefer value_range=(lo,hi) there.

nodes.label: D2 — Miller-Madow Correction + log(min(N,B)) Normalization
nodes.rationale: H_MM = H_plugin + (K-1)/(2N); H_norm = min(1, H_MM/log(min(N,B))). Denominator is log(min(N,B)) because at most min(N,B) bins can be non-empty (proof in D6). Miller-Madow makes deviation <=0.34% from N=128 up (exp2, gate A4 <5%). Clamp min(1,.) is a declared pragmatic choice to keep the [0,1] scale required by A6 — a documented blind zone of width ~(B-1)/(2N)/log B exists near the ceiling; users needing to distinguish ceiling values should use raw nats.

nodes.label: D2 — Reliability Criterion (reliable flag)
nodes.rationale: reliable iff (B-1)/(2N) <= 0.05*log(min(N,B)) — an a-priori, data-independent worst-case first-order bias check (N>=90 at B=32; uses B-1 not K-1 to be evaluable before seeing data). Adversarial verification (400-seed cells) proved it NECESSARY, NOT sufficient: lognormal sigma=2 and 90% zero-inflated data read True with 7-14% error at N in [90,~200]; all probed adversarial cases fall under 5% from N>=256; B=8 miscalibrated for heavy tails up to N~512. Honest flag semantics: True = no a-priori alarm from the bin-count bias model, not a certification. Zero-inflated case frozen as regression test. Open user decision (rule 05): whether to raise the default threshold.

nodes.label: D3 — Negative-Value Strategies (relu/abs, shift removed)
nodes.rationale: Strategy must be explicit because relu/abs answers differ up to 8.6x on the same input (anchor 0.0856 vs 0.7362). 'shift' REMOVED: no theoretical motivation and it annihilates constant rows (the maximum-entropy case) into an undefined result. Table: ReLU-family/Sigmoid -> relu (output non-negative by construction); GELU/SiLU/LeakyReLU -> relu (bounded negative range codes 'almost off', with documented 15-24% mass caveat at sigma~1); Tanh/Softsign/Hardtanh -> abs (sign = direction, ~50% negative mass); Softmax -> entropy computed directly; unmapped modules raise an explicit error with options listed — no silent default.

nodes.label: D4 — Full-Pipeline Bootstrap CI (normal interval)
nodes.rationale: REOPENED and re-decided after adversarial verification: exp4 had validated the closed-form (Basharin) on a strictly easier problem (fixed bins); in the real pipeline quantile edges are re-estimated from the sample and that variance is invisible to the formula (min coverage 62.5%, stderr ratio 0.46-1.37 non-converging — structural deficit). Percentile bootstrap collapses at the entropy ceiling (min 4%); basic bootstrap min 31.5%; calibrated stderr inflation rejected on principle (no principled constant exists). Adopted: R=200 resamples of RAW values with edges re-estimated per replicate, normal interval H_MM +/- 1.96*sd_boot — only method >=85% on all cells (90.5-100%). Read as '>=85%, conservative'; validity N>=200 (N~400 under >90% sparsity, detected at runtime from the histogram with a warning); CI truncated to [0, log(min(N,B))]. API consequence: needs raw values, so BatchEntropy carries no per-batch stderr; CI is on-demand via confidence_interval(). Blind spot: degenerate sample -> sd_boot=0 -> zero-width CI; the reliability flag is complementary, not replaceable. Per-example entropy has NO sampling stderr (deterministic function of the row).

nodes.label: D5 — Edge-Case Policies
nodes.rationale: Fail loud, never mask: N=0, NaN or +/-Inf input -> immediate ValueError (entropy undefined; silent handling would hide bugs in the observed network); N=1 and degenerate -> H=0 with reliable=False + reason; all-zero per-example row -> NaN + valid mask (0 would lie); 4D+ conv tensors -> core ValueError, hooks/layers skip the layer with an explicit warning (conv not validated in v1); 1D input treated as (N,1). New note 2026-07-13 (surfaced writing the numpy mirror, see D7): torch core checks isfinite on the ORIGINAL dtype then downcasts to float32, so a finite float64 > ~3.4e38 silently becomes inf — open gap on the torch core, numpy mirror rejects it; alignment left to user decision (rule 05).

nodes.label: D6 — Bound Proofs (A1/A2)
nodes.rationale: Gibbs-inequality proofs: batch-wise 0 <= H <= log(min(N,B)) via H <= log K = D_KL argument and K <= min(N,B); per-example 0 <= H <= log M with H=0 iff one-hot, H=log M iff uniform, S=0 -> declared NaN (D5). Attainability verified in exp5 (N<=B distinct bins -> log N exactly; N>B with B|N -> log B). Under default winsorization the max drops to 99.92% of log B for continuous uniform density only — with mass on B discrete levels log B stays exactly attainable (scoping in D1).

nodes.label: D7 — Numpy Reference Core (mirror, gated equivalence)
nodes.rationale: No new formulas — D1-D6 unchanged. entropylens/core_np.py replicates the torch core in numpy float32 so TF/JAX backends need no torch; only non-bitwise-guaranteed operations are quantiles (np.quantile vs torch.quantile, both linear interpolation) and reduction sum order. Equivalence gated in exp6 (torch 2.8.0+cpu / numpy 2.3.3 / Python 3.13): G1 counts bitwise + identical degenerate mask, G1b value_range branch, G2 max |dH| 4.77e-07 (gate 1e-5) and |dnormalized| 1.79e-07 (gate 5e-6), G3 reliable/reason identical, G4 per-example max |dH| 7.15e-07 with identical NaN positions, G5 CI half-width relative gap 0.060 (gate 10%) with pooled coverage 0.938. API consequence: numpy CI takes rng: np.random.Generator instead of torch.Generator — CI equivalence is statistical, NOT bitwise. core_np imports no torch/tensorflow/jax (AST test E2). Documented divergence: core_np validates finiteness AFTER the float32 cast, so float64 inputs that overflow to inf are rejected — intentionally stricter than the torch core.

nodes.label: D8 — Per-Backend Capture Semantics (TF aux model / JAX capture_intermediates)
nodes.rationale: TF: weight-sharing auxiliary keras.Model(model.inputs[0], {name: layer.output}) because Keras has no forward hooks — shares layer objects (exp7 G4 identity) and never touches the user model. Documented cost: one extra forward per observation in training=False, so BatchNorm/Dropout observations differ from the training pass (exp7 G5 is a NEGATIVE anchor: the expected outcome is the difference). Subclassed models (no model.inputs) unsupported in v1: explicit error, no silent fallback. JAX/Flax: capture_intermediates in the SAME forward (no second pass), mutable collection outside the grad path (exp8 G3). Captured Dense outputs are PRE-activation (flax activations are functions, not modules — exp8 G4): no strategy table is possible, per-example requires an explicit per-path strategy_map (consistent with D3: no silent default); unmapped paths tracked batch-wise only with a one-time-per-path warning (amended: the warning states per-example needs a strategy_map entry). Structural note: the __call__ marker recurs at every nesting level — the path walker must filter it recursively; leaves are 1-tuples of arrays. Version floors must cite VERIFIED pairs (TF 2.21.0/Keras 3.14, JAX 0.10.0/Flax 0.12.7): flax 0.8.0 + recent jax is broken at import.

nodes.label: D9 — Per-Backend Invariance Guarantee Scope
nodes.rationale: PyTorch: B1/B2/B3 bitwise via hooks (unchanged, existing tests). TensorFlow: user model NEVER touched => outputs and gradients invariant BY CONSTRUCTION; frozen bitwise (baseline before aux construction, observe between 3 SGD steps) with enable_op_determinism (exp7 G2/G3, TF 2.21.0). JAX/Flax: outputs and gradients bitwise with/without capture, without jit AND under jax.jit (max |d| = 0.00e+00, exp8 G1-G3). Honest jit scoping: G2 compares two INDEPENDENTLY jit-compiled closures (the real usage pattern) on CPU, stable over 5 reruns — empirical evidence on these pinned versions, NOT a JAX language guarantee; a jaxlib/XLA bump can change fusion/reduction order, so exp8 must be re-run on every jax/flax pin update. Common caveat: TF observation is inference-mode (D8) — a different measurement semantics vs the training step, not an invariance weakness.

nodes.label: Adversarial Verification (multi-agent review)
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent adversarial review of the decision document (2026-07-10). Incorporated outcomes: D4 reopened and re-decided (closed-form failed its own gate on the real pipeline -> exp4b full-pipeline bootstrap); D6/D1 winsorized-max formula corrected for asymmetric quantiles (mass summed to 1.04 under q=(0.05,0.99)); D5 N=0 row added; D2 reliability flag re-scoped to necessary-not-sufficient with H* ceiling scoping and heavy-tail caveats.

nodes.label: Validation Experiments (exp1–exp8, frozen evidence)
nodes.rationale: Frozen pre-implementation numeric evidence in validation/: exp1-exp5 + exp4b for D1-D6 (all PASS 2026-07-10, torch 2.8.0+cpu, Python 3.13) and exp6-exp8 backend gates for D7-D9 (added 2026-07-13, decided BEFORE implementation — same validation-first discipline). Every decision cites the numeric evidence that determined it; the scripts must stay green as part of the final gate.
